title: I've been testing a data screener for the last month to cut down my research time, actually surprised by the results
author: Murky_Meeting7208
selftext:
For context my guilty pleasure is typically deep doom scrolling niche finance blogs and pages to my girlfriends despair as I try and explain the Altman Z score to her. But I am a new father and my time as well as my ability to mess around with my portfolio is diminished between work and a crying child. 

I am on the same bandwagon as everyone else, eye-rolling anything claiming to be an "AI trading tool" because any 15 year old can use claude to make a moving average scanner. But now I don't have 3 hours a day to dig through sentiment data I had to sieve through some proper nonsense tools.

A month ago or so I started messing around with another, StockGPT, just to see if it could speed up my initial shortlisting for new picks. I kept it as a sounding board and used my own experience and judgement don't get me wrong, but I am actually impressed in how solid it has been so far.

In the tech dip it made the suggestion of MU (Micron), which surface level seems ridiculous but I am a sucker for a more contrarian suggestion so I looked into it, while sentiment towards it was in  the gutter the institutional volume and EPS projections were still strong (StockGPT highlighted the institutional vol and I dug and found the EPS projections), I took a position and rode correction and hit a 12 percent swing.

There could be potential here, I am not sure yet but I would love to know if anyone else has any other experience with the service and any others of similar style. I'd argue for shortening my initial research by a few hours it has been solid so far.
